transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess a few things, but... honestly, what really made me bring it up—or, well, what made my wife push me to bring it up—is that for the past few weeks, my eating has just been completely off. I mean, I’ll wake up and I just don't even think about food. I'll skip breakfast entirely, and then lunch rolls around and I’m still not hungry, so I just skip that without even meaning to. And it's not like I'm trying to diet or anything. I just don't have the desire to eat. Then dinner comes, and my wife—she's a great cook, she really is, she makes these amazing meals—she'll put a plate in front of me and I just sort of pick at it. I move the food around, take a couple of bites, but I just can't bring myself to finish it. It's frustrating for her, I know, because she put in all that effort. And I've noticed my jeans are starting to feel loose, like I'm having to pull my belt a notch tighter than usual. I just don't know why I don't want to eat. It's been like this for weeks now.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

No, no, not at all. That's the thing, I haven't been trying to diet or anything like that. I actually used to really enjoy eating. My wife and I, we used to go out to this little Italian place down the street on Fridays, and I'd always get the chicken parm, clean my plate, maybe even have some tiramisu after. But now? I couldn't even imagine eating half of that. It's just... the thought of food doesn't even cross my mind. I'm not looking at the scale, I'm not counting calories, I'm not trying to fit into an old pair of jeans or anything. It's more like my body just forgot that it needs food to function. I'll be sitting on the couch, maybe watching TV or just staring out the window, and hours will go by, and it won't even occur to me that I should probably have a snack or something. It's really strange, because like I said, I'm a guy who usually appreciates a good meal, especially when my wife cooks. She made her famous pot roast the other night, the one with the carrots and potatoes that slow-cooks all day, and the whole house smelled amazing, but I just... I couldn't do it. I took maybe three bites and felt completely full, almost nauseous even. So no, definitely not trying to lose weight on purpose. It's just happening because I can't bring myself to eat.
Have you been feeling anxious, sad, or stressed about anything lately?

Well, I guess... sad is probably the right word, though it's more like a heaviness, you know? Like, most days lately, I'll wake up and there's just this flat, heavy feeling right from the start. It’s hard to even explain it to my wife. The apartment just feels too quiet, even when the TV is on or she's moving around in the kitchen. Usually, I'd pick up my guitar—I've been playing since I was in high school, just acoustic stuff, some fingerpicking, nothing crazy, but it was always my way to sort of wake up my brain and get the day going. I've got this old Martin that has the best tone, and normally just strumming a few chords makes me feel centered. But lately? I look at it sitting there on the stand in the corner of the living room, and I just... I don't even want to touch it. And if I do force myself to pick it up, it doesn't do anything for me. It doesn't lift me up or make me feel any better. It's just wood and strings. Everything just feels sort of gray and pointless, like I'm dragging myself through the day with this weight on my chest. I don't know if there's a specific reason for it, like a big stressful event or anything like that. I just feel incredibly down, and it's been sticking with me almost every single day. It's exhausting, honestly, just feeling so empty all the time.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy besides playing guitar?

Well... I don't really think so. I mean, the guitar was really my main thing, you know? It’s the one hobby I did every single day without fail. Back when I was taking some college classes a few years ago, I even played in this little acoustic duo at a coffee shop near campus, so it’s just always been this huge part of my identity. That's why it feels so massive to not care about it right now. 

But as for other stuff... honestly, I haven't really noticed anything else dropping off like that. Like, I still watch TV with my wife in the evenings. We’ve been making our way through this really long documentary series on the national parks—she loves nature stuff—and I still follow along with that just fine, I still care about what we're watching. And I still like sitting out on the porch in the mornings, even if I’m not eating breakfast, just watching the neighborhood wake up and the cars drive by. I used to read a bit, mostly these old, pulpy sci-fi paperbacks from the 70s with the crazy cover art, and I guess I haven't picked one of those up in a minute, but that’s really just because I haven't found a good author lately, not because of this heavy feeling. 

So, yeah, I think it really is just the guitar that stands out. It’s just so glaring because it used to be my morning ritual, my way to clear my head before the day started, and now it’s just sitting there gathering dust. But I can't really think of any other specific hobbies or anything that I've completely stopped caring about.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling?

Gosh, let me think about that. It's kind of hard to pinpoint an exact day, you know? Because it doesn't just hit you all at once like catching a cold or something where you wake up and suddenly you're sick. It sort of sneaks up on you, really gradually. But if I really sit and look back at it, trying to trace it to when I first started feeling this... this slowed-down, depressed sort of pattern... I'd say it's been hanging around off and on for about three months now. 

Yeah, probably three months. Because I remember back around then, my wife and I were talking about doing some rearranging in the living room, maybe moving the couch and the TV stand to open up the space, and I just kept putting it off and putting it off because I felt that same heaviness starting to creep in. I just couldn't get the momentum going. But back then, it wasn't every single day. It was more like, I'd have a couple of days where I felt like I was wading through mud, just totally flat, and then I'd bounce back a little and feel somewhat normal again. Maybe I'd even pick up the guitar for a few minutes and play a song or two. So it was really off and on for a while there, playing hide and seek with me. I'd almost convince myself it was just a passing funk or that I was just having a lazy weekend. 

But recently? Man, it's just settled in completely. I'd say the past few weeks have definitely been the most noticeable. It's like the 'off and on' part stopped, and now it's just 'on' all the time. These last few weeks especially, there's no break from it. The heaviness is just there from the second I open my eyes, and it doesn't lift, no matter what I do or what's going on around the apartment. It's just this constant, dragging weight, making everything feel so incredibly slow.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over these past few weeks?

Well, you know, it's funny you ask that, because I actually was just thinking about this the other day. I haven't officially stepped on a scale or anything—we have one of those digital ones tucked under the bathroom sink, but I honestly can't remember the last time I pulled it out. But... yeah, I definitely think I've lost some weight. And what made me really notice it, what actually made me bring it up in my own head, is that for the past few weeks, my eating has just been completely off. 

It's not even like I'm actively trying to diet or anything like that. It's just... I'll wake up with that heavy feeling I was telling you about, and the thought of food just doesn't even register. So I'll skip breakfast completely. And then I'll just be sitting around, maybe watching TV or just staring out the window, and suddenly it's two or three in the afternoon, and I realize I haven't had lunch either. I just do it without even meaning to. My stomach doesn't rumble, I don't get cravings... nothing. 

And then dinner rolls around, and my wife—she's a really good cook, she makes these amazing casseroles and stews, especially now that the weather's turning—she'll put a plate in front of me, and I just... I just pick at it. Even when it smells great and I know it tastes good, I'll maybe take three or four bites, push it around the plate a bit, and I just can't finish it. It's like the physical act of eating is just too much effort, or my stomach just feels full after practically nothing. 

So because of all that, yeah, I've definitely noticed a physical change. Like, my favorite pair of jeans—the ones I usually wear around the apartment because they're broken in just right—they're starting to feel really loose around the waist. I'm having to pull my belt a notch tighter than I used to, which is weird for me because my weight usually stays pretty consistent. So, even without the scale, I can tell I'm definitely dropping pounds, just because I have zero interest in eating lately.
Would you say you've lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past month?

Well, like I was saying, it's hard to put an exact number on it since I haven't been using the scale. Five percent... I mean, I guess if I'm normally around, say, 180 pounds, five percent would be... what, like nine pounds? Honestly, yeah, I think it could easily be that much, maybe even more. 

Because, like I mentioned, what really made me bring it up in my own head is just how completely off my eating has been for the past few weeks. It's not just a skipped meal here and there. I'll wake up with that heaviness, and I'll skip breakfast entirely. And then I'll just be sitting there, maybe watching the cars go by, and suddenly it's three o'clock and I realize I haven't had lunch either, and I did it without even meaning to. My stomach just doesn't send any signals. 

And then dinner... my wife, she's such a great cook, she makes these amazing meals, but I just pick at them. Even when she makes my favorite stuff, I'll take a few bites and just push it around the plate. I just can't finish it. It's like I get full instantly, or the effort of chewing and swallowing is just too much. 

So with all of that going on every single day for weeks, yeah, the weight is definitely dropping off. Like I said, my jeans—the ones I wear all the time because they're perfectly broken in—they're really loose now. I'm having to cinch my belt tighter just to keep them up, which is totally new for me. So even without the official weigh-in, I'd say yeah, it's very likely I've lost more than five percent, just based on how my clothes fit and how little I've been eating.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Man, that's... that's a really tough question to think about, to be honest. Because I've been trying to find something, anything, that gives me a little spark, and... I just draw a complete blank. 

Like I was mentioning earlier about the guitar—I have this really beautiful acoustic, a Martin, that my dad gave me back when I was taking some college classes in my early twenties. I used to pick it up practically every single day. I'd sit on the edge of the bed and just strum for hours, trying to learn new fingerpicking patterns or just playing old folk songs, and I'd totally lose track of time because I was just so into it. But now? I look at it sitting there on the stand in the corner of the bedroom, and it just looks like... I don't know, just wood and wire. It doesn't even tempt me. I actually tried picking it up last week, thinking maybe if I just forced myself to play one chord, it would spark something, you know? Like jump-starting a car. But I just sat there holding it for about five minutes, feeling absolutely nothing, and then I put it back. 

And it's not just the guitar, either. It's really everything. Even dumb, easy stuff, like video games. I used to love firing up the PlayStation and just losing myself in a big open-world game for a whole afternoon, getting really invested in the story and the characters. My wife would even sit and watch me play sometimes because the graphics are so good now, they're practically like movies. But lately, I'll turn the console on, look at the menu screen with all my games lined up, and the thought of actually starting one just feels exhausting. It's like, what's the point? 

Even watching TV or movies with my wife... we used to have these great movie nights every Friday, where we'd make a big bowl of popcorn, get all cozy on the couch under a blanket, and really get into whatever we were watching. Now I just sit there staring at the screen and I'm not even following the plot. The colors just flash by, people are talking, but I'm not absorbing any of it. It's like the color and the flavor have just been completely drained out of every single thing I used to like doing. So, no, if I'm being completely honest, I really can't think of a single activity right now that actually brings me any enjoyment. It's all just totally flat.
How long have you felt like you couldn't enjoy the things you used to like doing?

Man, trying to put a timeline on it is... it's tricky, because time just kind of blurs together when you're feeling like this. It wasn't like a light switch, you know? It didn't just happen overnight where I woke up and suddenly the guitar meant nothing to me. 

If I really sit and look back, try to trace it to when things started feeling gray... I'd say I’ve had this depressed, really slowed-down pattern hanging around off and on for about three months now. Yeah, roughly three months. At first, it wasn't an everyday thing. I'd have a couple of days where I just didn't feel like doing much, maybe I'd leave the PlayStation off for a weekend and just lie on the couch, but then I'd bounce back a little bit. Or I'd think, "Oh, I'm just tired, I just need to rest." You always try to rationalize it, right? You tell yourself you're just in a funk or you're just burnt out. But then the funk just... it never really left. It just kept coming and going, just sort of hovering over me in the background. 

But if we're talking about this total flatline I'm in right now, where absolutely nothing sounds good? The past few weeks are definitely when it’s been the most noticeable. That's when it really settled in heavy. It just escalated from this off-and-on sluggishness over the last three months into this complete brick wall over the last few weeks, where I can't even fake it through a Friday movie night with my wife. So it's been building for a while, but lately, it's just impossible to ignore.
How long have you felt like you couldn't enjoy the things you used to like doing?

Well, yeah, kind of like I was just getting at... looking back on it, I’ve had this depressed, really slowed-down pattern hanging around off and on for about three months now. 

It’s hard to pinpoint the exact day it started because it’s sneaky, you know? About three months ago, it was more like this shadow that would just sort of come and go. I’d have a few days where I felt like I was walking through wet cement, just totally drained and not really caring about much, but then it would lift just enough that I'd think I was fine. You know how you try to explain things away to yourself? I kept telling my wife, "Oh, I just need better sleep," or "I'm just a little burnt out right now." I was constantly making excuses for why I didn't want to do anything. 

But it never fully went away. It just kept lingering in the background. And then, really, the past few weeks are when it’s been the most noticeable. It stopped being this off-and-on thing and just became... constant. It's like the volume just got turned all the way up. These last few weeks, that slowed-down feeling just completely took over and flattened absolutely everything. That's when it got to the point where I couldn't even look at my guitar or care about anything at all. So, yeah, roughly three months total of it creeping around, but the last few weeks are when it really set in heavy.
How long have you been feeling this constant, heavy emptiness without any breaks?

Without any breaks... yeah, that is exactly it. The unbroken part is what really gets to you. If we are talking about this current stretch, this specific low where it has just been a solid, heavy wall of nothing with zero relief... that has been going on for right about three weeks now. 

And I know exactly why I can pinpoint it to three weeks, because it lines up perfectly with when my wife finally settled into her full-time work schedule. She had been doing this sort of transitional, part-time thing before that, working some weird hours, so her schedule was a bit all over the place but she was around the house a lot more. I had gotten really used to that rhythm, having her presence there, even if she was just in the other room doing paperwork or whatever. 

But then, about three weeks ago, she officially shifted into the permanent, full-time hours. Out the door early in the morning, gone all day, back in the evening. And do not get me wrong, I am incredibly proud of her, it is a really good thing for us, but man, the house just got so incredibly quiet. Once she settled into that routine and was gone all day, every single day, that is when this heavy emptiness just dropped right on top of me and hasn't let up for a single second. 

It is like, before, when her schedule was lighter, I could kind of piggyback on her energy a little bit, or just the distraction of her being around kept me from sinking all the way down. But once she started the full-time grind three weeks ago, it has just been me and this... this void. I even tried setting an alarm the first few days of her new schedule, thinking I would get up when she gets up, make the coffee, keep some kind of momentum going for myself. But by the third day, I was just standing in the kitchen staring at the wall, feeling completely hollowed out. So yeah, exactly three weeks of this constant, unbroken low, right from the moment her new schedule locked in.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss recently, such as noticing your clothes are looser or you've lost a noticeable amount of weight without trying?

Yeah, actually, that is... that's kind of what made me start realizing how bad things were getting. Because for the past few weeks, my eating has just been completely off. And I'm not on a diet or anything, it's just happening. I will wake up and completely skip breakfast, and then the whole day goes by and I skip lunch, too, entirely without meaning to. It's not like I'm sitting there starving and refusing to eat, it's just... the thought of food, the effort of getting up and making something, it just doesn't even cross my mind. I just sit there in that quiet house and the day just slips by. 

And then in the evenings, my wife will come home from her new job, and she'll actually take the time to cook for us. She'll make a really nice meal, something I usually love, and put a plate right in front of me. But even then, with the food right there, I just end up picking at it. I push it around with my fork, take maybe a bite or two, and I'm just done. I feel awful because she worked all day and still cooked, you know? I want to eat it for her sake, but my stomach just doesn't want it. 

And because of all that missed food over these last few weeks, yeah, my clothes are definitely fitting differently. I put on my go-to pair of jeans a couple of days ago, and they are starting to feel really loose around the waist. I'm having to pull my belt a notch tighter just to keep them sitting right. So I haven't actually stepped on a scale to see the exact number of pounds I've dropped, but losing weight without trying? Yeah, the jeans don't lie. It's definitely happening.
How long have you noticed your clothes feeling looser due to weight loss?

Well, like I was saying, it's really been over the course of these past few weeks, you know, right around the time my wife started that full-time schedule. Because before that, when she was around more, we were eating pretty normally. She'd make sure we had lunch, or we'd grab something together. But once she transitioned to those long hours and I started skipping breakfast and lunch entirely... that's when it started. 

I guess I first really took notice of the clothes thing just a couple of days ago with those jeans I mentioned. But thinking about it, the actual weight loss must have been happening gradually over this whole three-week stretch of not eating. It's not like I woke up one day and suddenly everything was baggy, you know? It's more like... I'd put on a t-shirt and think, "Huh, this feels a little drafty," or I'd notice my sweatpants were sitting a little lower on my hips than usual when I was just lounging around the house. But you don't really put two and two together right away. You just think maybe the laundry stretched them out or something. 

But then, yeah, a couple of days ago, I had to actually put on real pants—those jeans—because I had to go outside to grab the mail and the neighbor was out there, and I didn't want to be standing there in my pajamas at two in the afternoon. And when I buttoned them, there was this huge gap. I could fit my whole hand down the waistband. And that's when it really hit me, like, "Wow, I am actually losing a lot of weight." So the realization was recent, just a few days ago, but the actual process of losing it and the clothes slowly getting looser... that's been happening steadily over the last three weeks since my eating habits just completely fell off a cliff.
How many weeks have you noticed a significant difference in your weight?

Well, like I've been saying, it really all ties back to this current low stretch I've been in. The whole thing, the weight loss, the not eating, the emptiness... it's all been going on for about three weeks now. 

It's just so strange how you can pinpoint these things, you know? Because I can trace it back exactly to when my wife settled into her full-time work schedule. Before that, when she was doing the part-time, transitional hours, my weight was totally fine. I mean, my pants fit, I wasn't needing to tighten my belt, I was eating the lunches she'd make or we'd scrounge up together. But the second she shifted into those permanent, long hours and was gone all day... that was three weeks ago. And that's exactly when this heavy, unbroken low started, and exactly when I stopped eating. 

So, I mean, if you're asking how many weeks I've actually noticed the difference... I guess the physical proof, like the jeans falling off me, really just clicked a few days ago. But the actual weight loss itself, the process of it happening because I haven't been eating? That's been the full three weeks. It's just been this steady decline right alongside my mood, ever since the house got so quiet when she started working those full-time hours. Three solid weeks of just... shrinking, I guess. Both mentally and physically.
How long have you felt like you couldn't enjoy playing the guitar?

Well, the guitar thing... it's really tied into this whole mood I've been in lately. It's been happening for about the same amount of time, these last three weeks since my wife went full-time. 

You see, playing guitar used to be my thing. I've got this beautiful acoustic, a Taylor, that I saved up for years to buy back when I was still taking some classes. And usually, I'd pick it up every day. It was my way to unwind, or to just kind of express whatever I was feeling. Even if I was just strumming some basic chords while watching TV, it felt good, you know? It was comforting. 

But lately... most days lately, I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling. It's hard to describe. It's just like... a weight on my chest, and the whole apartment just feels too quiet, too empty. And I'll look at the guitar sitting there on its stand in the corner of the living room, right where I always leave it, and I'll think, "Maybe I should play a little. Maybe that will help." And sometimes I'll even go over and pick it up. I'll sit down on the couch, rest it on my knee, put my fingers on the fretboard... and then just nothing. 

It doesn't lift me up at all anymore. There's no spark, no joy in it. I'll strum a G chord and it just sounds like noise. It feels like a chore, honestly. The physical act of pressing down the strings just feels exhausting, and the music doesn't make me feel anything. It's just flat, like everything else right now. So I end up just putting it back on the stand after a minute or two and going back to just sitting there in the quiet. It's really frustrating because I want to enjoy it, I really do, but that heavy feeling just swallows it all up. So, yeah, it's been about three weeks of just... not being able to find any comfort in it at all.
Have you felt this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah, yeah, it really has been. It's... it's been pretty much every single day for these last three weeks, and it really does last for most of the day. 

Like I was saying before, most days lately I just wake up with this heavy, flat feeling. It's almost like a physical weight, you know? Like gravity is just pulling on me harder than it used to. And it starts right from the moment I open my eyes. I'll lie there in bed, and I can hear the hum of the refrigerator or maybe a car driving by outside, but otherwise, the apartment is just so quiet. Too quiet. And that heavy feeling just settles right in. 

And it doesn't really lift as the day goes on. I'll drag myself out of bed, maybe wander into the living room, and that's when I'll look at the guitar. And like I mentioned, I'll think, "Okay, maybe if I just play a little, maybe if I just do something I usually love, this fog will lift." But it doesn't. Even picking up my guitar doesn't really lift me. I'll sit there with it, and it's just... nothing. The whole day just stretches out in front of me like this long, gray road, and I just feel completely flat. 

It's not just a passing mood, you know? It's not like I get sad for an hour and then snap out of it. It's this constant, lingering heaviness that just sits on my chest from morning until night, day after day. So, yes, to answer your question, it's absolutely been most of the day, nearly every day, for well over two weeks now. It's been the full three weeks since my wife went full-time, just this unbroken stretch of feeling completely weighed down and empty.
Have you felt this way for at least two weeks?

Well, yes, definitely for the last two weeks. I mean, the really heavy, unbroken stretch, the part where I can't even pick up the guitar or eat, that's been the last three weeks, like I said. But if I'm really being honest, and I've been thinking about this a lot while I've just been sitting around the apartment... if I really look back at the whole picture, this depressed, slowed-down pattern hasn't just been a three-week thing. 

It's actually been hanging around, off and on, for about three months now. It's just that it wasn't as constant before. Like, three months ago, I'd have a few days where I felt like I was moving through molasses, you know? Where my brain just felt thick and sluggish, and I didn't want to do much. But then maybe I'd have a decent day, or my wife would be home more, and it would kind of lift a little bit, enough that I could ignore it. 

But it was always kind of there, lurking in the background. A few days of feeling heavy and slow, then maybe a day of feeling okay, and then back to the heaviness. It's just that these past few weeks, since the schedule change, it's like someone turned the dial all the way up and snapped off the knob. The past three weeks are definitely when it's been the most noticeable, the most impossible to ignore, because it just hasn't stopped. But the actual pattern of feeling this way? Yeah, that's been dragging on for a solid three months, just kind of ebbing and flowing until it finally settled into this current low.
Have you experienced any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation during these past three weeks?

No, no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I know it probably sounds really bleak when I talk about the heavy feeling and the gray road and all that, but it's not... it hasn't gone to that kind of dark place. I don't want to die, or anything like that. 

It's more just this intense frustration with being awake and feeling this way, if that makes sense? But not wanting to actually end my life. Like, I'll be sitting there on the couch, right? Just staring at the coffee table or the turned-off TV, and the apartment is just so incredibly silent since my wife is at her new full-time schedule, and I just feel completely hollowed out. But my brain never goes to 'I should just end this.' It's more like, 'How long am I going to have to sit here feeling like a sack of lead?' 

I think about my wife a lot during those hours, too. She's out there working so hard for us right now, putting in all those hours, and I'm just stuck here in the living room unable to even strum a few chords on my guitar. It makes me feel bad, sure, that I'm just sitting around, but I would never, ever want to put her through something horrific like me hurting myself. I love her way too much for that. So, even though this fog is just so thick and I feel like I'm not really living a full life right now, just sort of existing in the quiet... I definitely haven't had any thoughts of death or suicide. It's just a really deep, heavy emptiness that I'm just... waiting to pass, I guess.
Has this heavy, empty feeling you've been describing lasted for at least two weeks straight without any improvement?

Yeah, like I was saying a few minutes ago, it's definitely been longer than two weeks. It's funny, you know, how time kind of blurs together when you're just sitting in the exact same spot on the couch all day, just watching the dust motes float in the sunlight coming through the blinds. You really start to lose track of whether it's Tuesday or Thursday because every single day has that exact same heavy, empty quality to it, just stretching out in front of you. 

But I can pinpoint the timeline pretty exactly because of my wife's job. This current low stretch—this really unbroken, heavy part where there hasn't been any improvement at all, where I just feel totally hollowed out—it's been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after she really settled into her new full-time work schedule. 

Before that, you know, like I mentioned earlier, there were those three months where it was kind of ebbing and flowing, a few bad days and then a passable one. But once she made that transition and started being gone all day, every day, leaving me alone in the quiet apartment... that's when this current stretch really just locked in and threw away the key. So, yes, it's been a solid three weeks straight of just... nothing lifting. Not even a crack of light through the fog since she started those full-time hours.

Even picking up my guitar doesn't really lift me. I'll sit there with it, and it's just... nothing. The whole day just stretches out in front of me like this long, gray road, and I just feel completely flat. 

It's not just a passing mood, you know? It's not like I get sad for an hour and then snap out of it. It's this constant, lingering heaviness that just sits on my chest from morning until night, day after day. So, yes, to answer your question, it's absolutely been most of the day, nearly every day, for well over two weeks now. It's been the full three weeks since my wife went full-time, just this unbroken stretch of feeling completely weighed down and empty.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's condition meets the duration criteria for a major depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you felt this way for at least two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, I’ve had this depressed, slowed-down pattern hanging around off and on for about three months, with the past few weeks feeling the most noticeable.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to confirm the duration of the depressive symptoms, allowing the patient to elaborate that the depressed, slowed-down pattern has actually been hanging around off and on for about three months.

patient.answer:
Well, yes, definitely for the last two weeks. I mean, the really heavy, unbroken stretch, the part where I can't even pick up the guitar or eat, that's been the last three weeks, like I said. But if I'm really being honest, and I've been thinking about this a lot while I've just been sitting around the apartment... if I really look back at the whole picture, this depressed, slowed-down pattern hasn't just been a three-week thing. 

It's actually been hanging around, off and on, for about three months now. It's just that it wasn't as constant before. Like, three months ago, I'd have a few days where I felt like I was moving through molasses, you know? Where my brain just felt thick and sluggish, and I didn't want to do much. But then maybe I'd have a decent day, or my wife would be home more, and it would kind of lift a little bit, enough that I could ignore it. 

But it was always kind of there, lurking in the background. A few days of feeling heavy and slow, then maybe a day of feeling okay, and then back to the heaviness. It's just that these past few weeks, since the schedule change, it's like someone turned the dial all the way up and snapped off the knob. The past three weeks are definitely when it's been the most noticeable, the most impossible to ignore, because it just hasn't stopped. But the actual pattern of feeling this way? Yeah, that's been dragging on for a solid three months, just kind of ebbing and flowing until it finally settled into this current low.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of the depression to differentiate between F32.0 and F32.1
doctor.question: Have you experienced any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation during these past three weeks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation or thoughts of death, which is not included in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I know it probably sounds really bleak when I talk about the heavy feeling and the gray road and all that, but it's not... it hasn't gone to that kind of dark place. I don't want to die, or anything like that. 

It's more just this intense frustration with being awake and feeling this way, if that makes sense? But not wanting to actually end my life. Like, I'll be sitting there on the couch, right? Just staring at the coffee table or the turned-off TV, and the apartment is just so incredibly silent since my wife is at her new full-time schedule, and I just feel completely hollowed out. But my brain never goes to 'I should just end this.' It's more like, 'How long am I going to have to sit here feeling like a sack of lead?' 

I think about my wife a lot during those hours, too. She's out there working so hard for us right now, putting in all those hours, and I'm just stuck here in the living room unable to even strum a few chords on my guitar. It makes me feel bad, sure, that I'm just sitting around, but I would never, ever want to put her through something horrific like me hurting myself. I love her way too much for that. So, even though this fog is just so thick and I feel like I'm not really living a full life right now, just sort of existing in the quiet... I definitely haven't had any thoughts of death or suicide. It's just a really deep, heavy emptiness that I'm just... waiting to pass, I guess.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's condition meets the duration criteria for a Major Depressive Episode
doctor.question: Has this heavy, empty feeling you've been describing lasted for at least two weeks straight without any improvement?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This current low stretch has been going on for about three weeks, starting after my wife settled into her full-time work schedule.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to confirm if the current depressed mood has lasted for at least two weeks straight, which corresponds to the 3-week duration of the current low stretch.

patient.answer:
Yeah, like I was saying a few minutes ago, it's definitely been longer than two weeks. It's funny, you know, how time kind of blurs together when you're just sitting in the exact same spot on the couch all day, just watching the dust motes float in the sunlight coming through the blinds. You really start to lose track of whether it's Tuesday or Thursday because every single day has that exact same heavy, empty quality to it, just stretching out in front of you. 

But I can pinpoint the timeline pretty exactly because of my wife's job. This current low stretch—this really unbroken, heavy part where there hasn't been any improvement at all, where I just feel totally hollowed out—it's been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after she really settled into her new full-time work schedule. 

Before that, you know, like I mentioned earlier, there were those three months where it was kind of ebbing and flowing, a few bad days and then a passable one. But once she made that transition and started being gone all day, every day, leaving me alone in the quiet apartment... that's when this current stretch really just locked in and threw away the key. So, yes, it's been a solid three weeks straight of just... nothing lifting. Not even a crack of light through the fog since she started those full-time hours.
